title: Software engineering
audience: a college student in a computer science degree program, or a career changer studying the same material on their own
purpose: Learn how teams build and maintain software: the software life cycle, requirements and user stories, design and modularity, UML class and sequence diagrams, version-control workflows, code review, testing strategy and test design, agile methods, estimation and planning, maintenance, refactoring and technical debt, documentation, and professional ethics.
primary_reading: Software Engineering at Google (free online book)

weeks.1: What software engineering is: process and life cycle
weeks.4: Modeling with UML: class and sequence diagrams
weeks.7: Testing strategy: unit, integration and system tests
weeks.8: Test design: equivalence classes and boundaries

blocks.deliverable: Write user stories with acceptance criteria.
Draw class and sequence diagrams for a feature.
Week 7 midterm; design test cases for a specification.
Refactor a code smell and document the change.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Team-style project (solo or with peers): take a supplied product brief through requirements, design, a sprint plan, the implementation of one feature with tests, a code review and a retrospective, delivered as a design document and working code.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
